simple: The full list of "this kernel, on this machine, with this many CPUs, running this test" combinations that must pass before a change is accepted.
analogy: The drill timetable: every drill, in every building, with every class size.
precise: A versioned file of rows, each naming an architecture, an emulator or machine configuration, a time limit and a pass rule (exit status and a required serial line); the harness runs every row from a clean build and the verdict is the conjunction of the counted rows. MP1's own definition, built on the curriculum's acceptance-test rules.
source: D1, D2 of MP1; R3 of MP1 (run in this build)

simple: The saved results of the last run everyone agreed was good, so a new run can be compared with it row by row.
analogy: Last term's drill record, kept on file.
precise: The results file of an accepted matrix run; a row that passed in the baseline and does not pass now (or is missing) is a regression, whatever the overall count says. MP1's own definition.
source: R8 of MP1 (run in this build)

simple: Writing down the time on the computer that runs the test whenever a line of boot output arrives.
analogy: One stopwatch held by the inspector, not by each school.
precise: The harness reads the guest's serial output line by line and records, for each line, the host's monotonic clock relative to the start of the run; stage durations are differences between these stamps. It includes the serial path and does not need the guest's clocks to be calibrated or comparable between operating systems.
source: R4, R12 of MP1 (runs in this build)

simple: One page listing every way your kernel is built or started differently on each machine, and why.
analogy: The one page added to the rule book: in the village school, the bell is a hand bell.
precise: A design note, kept under version control with the regression matrix, with one row per difference (image, build option, boot path, command line, devicetree or ACPI source, driver set) and its reason; the MP1 rubric's first criterion (one kernel image or a documented minimal difference) is graded against it.

simple: Typing commands on one computer and having them run on another, over the network.
analogy: The office window, reached by telephone from another building.
precise: A user-space server on the operating system that accepts a TCP connection, runs a shell with its standard input and output connected to the connection, and returns the output; the MP1 card accepts it, or a file service, as milestone 4.
